title: Escaping Reasoning Basin Collapse with History-Biased Search
topic: Probabilistic Methods->Monte Carlo and Sampling Methods
claim: Search concentrates visits on already-explored options, so effective diversity falls consistently below the number of distinct options explored.
layout: single scatter panel, diagonal reference line, shaded region below, highlighted mean marker
description: A single square scatter plot. The x-axis is the number of distinct reasoning basins (0 to 18). The y-axis is the effective basin count N_eff (0 to 18). A dashed black diagonal marks 'No redundancy' (N_eff = n_basins). The region below the diagonal is shaded light gray. Many semi-transparent points sit in vertical columns at integer x-values. Blue points are correct predictions and salmon-red points are incorrect ones, and the two overlap heavily. Every point lies on or below the diagonal, and the gap widens as n_basins grows. A large red diamond with a blue stripe marks the mean, near (8.5, 6.8). A legend sits at top left. A box at bottom right reads 'Mean N_eff/nodes = 0.38'. The eye goes first to the diagonal and the shaded region.
caption: Reasoning basin collapse in ToT. Each point is one MuSR problem (n=300, gpt-oss-120b). The y-axis shows Neff, the effective number of basins explored after accounting for visit concentration. All points fall below the diagonal (shaded), where Neff < nbasins, indicating that visits concentrate on previously explored basins.
abstract: Inference-time search with large language models (LLMs) often concentrates on a small set of structurally or semantically similar trajectories, leaving alternative reasoning strategies underexplored---a failure mode we call \textit{reasoning basin collapse}. We introduce \textsc{BASIN}, a training-free, history-biased search method that groups reasoning states into basins and accumulates a revisit penalty on repeatedly selected basins, reallocating a fixed inference budget toward underexplored reasoning strategies. Under matched inference budgets, \textsc{BASIN} improves over Tree of Thoughts (ToT) by up to $+22$pp on Game of 24 and $+6.7$pp on MuSR. Because indiscriminate diversification can over-explore once search has found a promising basin, we further introduce \textsc{QA-BASIN}, a quality-aware variant that weakens the revisit penalty for high-quality basins and yields more robust gains. To characterize when basin-aware search helps, we introduce the \emph{redundancy gap} $Î$, which measures the difference in search concentration between correct and incorrect predictions: standard ToT often operates near $Î\approx 0$, whereas \textsc{BASIN} consistently shifts $Î$ positive. Together, these results identify reasoning basin collapse as a failure mode of inference-time search and show that history-dependent bias provides a simple, training-free mechanism for escaping redundant reasoning under fixed compute. Code is available at https://github.com/GitHubLuCheng/basin
